question: A laboratory report ends with a value that is 2 times a converted reading, because two benches contribute equally. That converted reading is the kilojoule form of a figure obtained by subtracting a bearing allowance of 4 J and then a drag allowance of 7 J from the energy a carrier of 21000 grams holds because of its motion. The carrier's speed in metres per second is the total of the squares of the whole numbers from 1 to 4. What value, in kilojoules, ends the report?

A test report ends with a value found by taking a calibration credit of 2 kJ off a doubled total, the doubling being for the two rigs that run together. That doubled total is itself 10 times a converted single-shot reading, since 10 shots make a set. The converted reading is the kilojoule form of the energy a hammer of 14 kg carries because of its motion at impact, and the hammer's impact speed in metres per second is the larger of the two values of x for which x^2 - 9x + 14 = 0. The hammer hangs from a pivot 2 m above the anvil, a length the report never uses. What value, in kilojoules, ends the report?

A bench-top actuator accelerates a test carriage of 6 kg along a smooth rail. The carriage's acceleration in metres per second squared is the smaller of the two values of x for which x^2 - 9x + 20 = 0. The controller works out the force needed to drive the carriage and expresses it in kilonewtons. It multiplies that converted figure by 4, because 4 carriages run on the bench, and then by 12, because 12 benches are in service. What figure, in kilonewtons, does the controller report?

A drop rig in a materials laboratory releases a striker of 41 kg onto a target. The striker's speed at impact, in metres per second, is the larger of the two values of x for which x^2 - 15x + 56 = 0. The bench records the energy the striker carries because of its motion at that moment, then subtracts a guide-friction allowance of 8 J, adds a calibration offset of 7 J, and adds a further standing allowance of 24 J. The final figure is then expressed in kilojoules. What value, in kilojoules, does the bench report?

A machine-shop entry is 2 times an adjusted reading, because the shop runs two identical slides. The adjusted reading is the raw force less a frame tare of 2 N, and the raw force is what is needed to accelerate a tool head of 174000 grams. The acceleration in metres per second squared is found by taking the rate at which the slope of the fitted position curve 3x^3 - 4x^2 is itself changing at the instant x = 3 seconds, with x the time in seconds and the position in metres, and then adding a drive contribution of 18 to it. What number, in newtons, is the entry?

A quarry conveyor accelerates a rock tray of 173000 grams along its frame. The tray's acceleration in metres per second squared is the larger of the two values of x for which x^2 - 6x + 8 = 0. The control system works out the force needed to drive the tray and expresses it in kilonewtons. It multiplies that converted figure by 10 for the 10 trays on a conveyor, by 5 for the 5 conveyors at a site, and by 4 for the 4 sites in the group. What figure, in kilonewtons, does the control system report?

A launch bench brings a carriage of 39000 grams up to speed, and the carriage's acceleration in metres per second squared follows 3t^2 + 1t, with t the time in seconds. Between t = 2 seconds and t = 3 seconds the speed builds from rest at the start of that interval, and the speed reached at the end is the launch speed. The bench records the energy the carriage carries because of its motion at that speed and adds a fixed instrument offset of 14 J. The result is multiplied by 4 for the 4 carriages in a run, by 6 for the 6 runs in a session, and by 12 for the 12 sessions in the programme. What total, in joules, does the bench report?

A test summary ends with a figure that is 8 times a site value, because 8 sites run the same rig. Each site value is what you get by adding a standing allowance of 8 kJ and then a further handling allowance of 10 kJ to a converted reading. That converted reading is the kilojoule form of the energy a trolley of 29000 grams carries because of its motion, and the trolley's speed in metres per second is the smaller of the two values of x for which x^2 - 9x + 18 = 0. What figure, in kilojoules, ends the summary?

A workshop ledger closes with a number that is 9 times an adjusted value, since 9 benches contribute. The adjusted value is what you get by adding a calibration offset of 17 kJ to a figure from which a contractual credit of 26 kJ had already been subtracted. That figure is the kilojoule form of the energy a puck of 3 kg carries because of its motion, and the puck's speed in metres per second is 2 times the sum of 2 and 16. The bench is 1.6 m wide, a dimension the ledger never uses. What number, in kilojoules, closes the ledger?

A teaching rig launches a slider of 24000 grams along a level bench. The slider's launch speed in metres per second is worked out in stages: take the smaller of the two values of x for which x^2 - 10x + 21 = 0, subtract a spring loss of 19, add a drive contribution of 11, and add a further boost of 12. The bench then records the energy the slider carries because of its motion at that launch speed. What number, in joules, does the bench record?

A vibration laboratory fits the curve 1x^3 + 0x^2 to a recorded trace, with x the time in seconds. At the instant x = 2 seconds the rate at which the slope of that fitted curve is itself changing gives, in metres per second, the speed of a test mass of 53 kg on the shaker head. The bench records the energy the mass carries because of its motion and adds a calibration offset of 1 J. The result is multiplied by 4 for the 4 heads on the machine, and then by 12 for the 12 machines in the hall. What figure, in joules, does the bench report?

A test report ends with a value found by taking a calibration credit of 29 kJ off a figure that is 5 times a run total, and each run total is 9 times a converted single-launch reading. That converted reading is the kilojoule form of the energy a carriage of 59 kg carries because of its motion at the end of a launch. During a launch the carriage's acceleration in metres per second squared follows 4t^2 + 7t, and between t = 1 second and t = 2 seconds the speed builds from rest at the start of that interval to give the launch speed. The launch track is 45 m long, a dimension the report never uses. What value, in kilojoules, ends the report?

A laboratory figure is 4 times an adjusted reading, because 4 benches contribute. The adjusted reading is what you get by adding a fixed instrument offset of 22 J to a figure that is 5 times a single-run record, since 5 runs make a set. Each single-run record is the energy a slider of 59000 grams carries because of its motion at the end of the run. During a run the slider's acceleration in metres per second squared follows 2t^2 + 0t between t = 0 seconds and t = 1 second, starting from rest, with t the time in seconds. The bench is 1.1 m wide, a dimension never used here. What is the laboratory figure, in joules?

A haulage report ends with a number that is 5 times a converted total, because 5 depots report together. That converted total is the kilonewton form of a figure obtained by taking a coupling tare of 25 N off a rake total, and the rake total is 5 times the force needed to drive one wagon. Each wagon has a mass of 196000 grams, and its acceleration in metres per second squared is what the rate curve 4t^2 + 0t accumulates between t = 3 seconds and t = 4 seconds, starting from zero at t = 3 seconds, with t the time in seconds. What number, in kilonewtons, ends the report?

A demonstration bench launches a puck of 3 kg across a smooth surface. The puck's launch speed in metres per second is the smaller of the two values of x for which x^2 - 11x + 24 = 0. The bench records the energy the puck carries because of its motion and multiplies it by 7, because 7 launches make a demonstration. A fixed instrument offset of 8 J is added, the result is multiplied by 6 for the 6 demonstrations in the term, and a standing allowance of 4 J is added at the end. The bench is 1.2 m tall, a dimension that plays no part. What figure, in joules, does the bench report?

A plant figure is 7 times a line total, because 7 lines run the same job, and each line total is 12 times a converted station reading. The converted reading is the kilonewton form of the force needed to accelerate a carrier of 52 kg on one station. The acceleration in metres per second squared is the number of distinct pairs that can be chosen from the plant's 10 test masses. The plant floor is 45 m long, a dimension that never enters the calculation. What is the plant figure, in kilonewtons?

A crane yard lifts a module of 162000 grams along a guided rail. The module's acceleration in metres per second squared is the smaller of the two values of x for which x^2 - 14x + 48 = 0. The control system works out the force needed to drive the module and expresses it in kilonewtons, then multiplies that converted figure by 12 because 12 modules are handled in a cycle. A fixed rigging allowance of 3 kN is added to the cycle total, and the result is multiplied by 9 for the 9 cranes in the yard. What figure, in kilonewtons, does the control system report?

A rolling mill drives a slab carrier of 154000 grams along its bed. The rate at which the carrier's acceleration builds, in metres per second cubed, follows 5t^2 + 1t, and between t = 1 second and t = 3 seconds the acceleration accumulates from zero at the start of that interval, giving the acceleration the mill uses. From the force needed to drive the carrier the controller subtracts a bearing tare of 5 N, then multiplies the result by 10 because 10 carriers run together. The total is expressed in kilonewtons for the report. The mill bed is 18 m long, a dimension the controller never uses. What figure, in kilonewtons, does the controller report?

A workshop counts 264 washers in one tray and 358 in another, and the technician works out the largest whole number that divides both counts exactly with nothing left over. A carrier of 57000 grams is then launched along the rail at a speed, in metres per second, equal to that number. The bench records the energy the carrier holds because of its motion and expresses it in kilojoules. It adds a standing allowance of 15 kJ, subtracts a handling credit of 8 kJ, and multiplies what remains by 12 because 12 benches report together. What figure, in kilojoules, does the bench report?

A conveyor drive accelerates a crate of 62000 grams along the rollers. The acceleration in metres per second squared is worked out by taking the smaller of the two values of x for which x^2 - 9x + 14 = 0, adding a drive contribution of 5, and multiplying the result by 10 for the ten-stage gearbox. The controller works out the force needed to move the crate and expresses it in kilonewtons, then adds a fixed frame allowance of 1 kN. The roller bed is 6 m long, a dimension the controller never uses. What figure, in kilonewtons, does the controller report?

A laboratory report ends with a value that is 5 times a site figure, because 5 laboratories report together. Each site figure is what you get by adding a standing instrument allowance of 29 kJ to a converted reading. That converted reading is the kilojoule form of the energy a glider of 38 kg carries because of its motion along the air track, and the glider's speed in metres per second is the smaller of the two values of x for which x^2 - 10x + 24 = 0. The track is 2 m long, a dimension the report never uses. What value, in kilojoules, ends the report?

A launch bench brings a carriage of 31 kg up to speed along a level rail, and the carriage's acceleration in metres per second squared follows 5t^2 + 7t, with t the time in seconds. Between t = 1 second and t = 3 seconds the speed builds from rest at the start of that interval, and the speed reached at the end is the launch speed. The bench records the energy the carriage carries because of its motion at that speed and expresses it in kilojoules. The converted figure is multiplied by 3 for the 3 carriages in a run, by 7 for the 7 runs in a session, and by 2 for the 2 sessions in the study. The rail is 25 m long, a length the bench never uses. What total, in kilojoules, does the bench report?

A calibration rig holds 13 identical reference masses, and the acceleration it applies, in metres per second squared, is the number of distinct pairs that can be chosen from them. That acceleration is given to a shuttle of 5000 grams on the rig's rail. The controller records the force needed to drive the shuttle and multiplies it by 3, because the routine runs on 3 axes, then expresses the result in kilonewtons. A fixed frame allowance of 21 kN is added to the converted figure, and the sum is multiplied by 2 because two rigs run the routine together. What number, in kilonewtons, does the controller report?

A test plant keeps 10 identical reference masses, and the acceleration its rig applies, in metres per second squared, is the number of distinct pairs that can be chosen from them. That acceleration is given to a carrier of 121000 grams. The controller records the force needed to drive the carrier, multiplies it by 4 because 4 carriers run together, and expresses the result in kilonewtons. The converted figure is then multiplied by 12 for the 12 rigs in the plant, and a fixed frame allowance of 3 kN is added at the end. The plant floor is 30 m long, a dimension the controller never uses. What number, in kilonewtons, does the controller report?

A test-bed ledger closes with a number that is 15 kN more than a figure from which a contractual credit of 8 kN had already been subtracted. That figure is the kilonewton form of the force needed to accelerate a slide of 129 kg. The slide's acceleration in metres per second squared is what the rate curve 2t^2 + 0t accumulates between t = 0 seconds and t = 3 seconds, starting from zero, with t the time in seconds. The test bed is 10 m long, a dimension the ledger never uses. What number, in kilonewtons, closes the ledger?
